facts.fact: In July 2026 the Ministry of Health and the Ministry of Basic and Secondary Education signed an MoU to link the HMIS with the EMIS so that immunisation, nutrition, screening and birth registration data can be shared with education indicators; the story describes this as to be integrated, with a joint working group set up.

The World Bank ISR for the RISE project records a current value of 0 systems interoperable at 25 November 2025 across the GamSR, education management information systems, CRVS and the health insurance system, with one instance being verified and a target of at least 3 by October 2028.
facts.system: Health insurance system (interoperability indicator of the RISE project)

note: The only health system named is the health insurance system, inside a cross-sector indicator; no pair of health systems is named.
The passages are only the title, abbreviations and contents of a 2019 social registry design report; they state nothing about health systems exchanging data.

facts.fact: Atlantic Infos reports that WAHO opened a five-day regional workshop in Cotonou to pilot automated transfer of routine health data from national DHIS2 systems, with Gambia one of four pilot countries.
facts.system: WAHO automated routine health data sharing (DHIS2)

systems.system: WAHO automated routine health data sharing (DHIS2)
